accept: chronic aortic regurgitation with left ventricular dilatation

findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy with volume overload pattern

echoTasks.find: Dilated left ventricle with hyperdynamic motion and a diastolic colour jet across the valve
Dense diastolic jet with rapid deceleration on continuous wave Doppler
Markedly dilated left ventricle with a wide jet origin in the apical window

auscultation.added: Austin Flint rumble at the apex in severe disease
auscultation.murmur: Early diastolic decrescendo murmur grade 3 of 4 at the left sternal edge

exam.general: Young man, tall, breathless on exertion, visible carotid pulsation
exam.other: Quincke pulse in the nail beds, Duroziez sign over the femoral artery, lungs clear
exam.precordium: Displaced hyperdynamic apex beat with a diastolic thrill at the base
exam.pulse: Collapsing 78 with a wide pulse pressure of 105 mmHg

history.a: Breathless on playing cricket for 8 months, aware of heartbeat at night
history.q: Exercise tolerance and awareness of heartbeat

history.a: No chest pain, no fainting, occasional head throbbing with the pulse
Murmur noted at school entry, never followed up
No hypertension, no diabetes, no drugs
Engineering student, plays cricket, worried about sports clearance
No family heart disease, parents healthy

keyPoints: Refer to the heart team for aortic valve surgery assessment, as severe disease with dilatation meets operative criteria
Control systolic hypertension to reduce regurgitant load while preserving diastolic pressure
Counsel against competitive endurance sport until the surgical plan is set
Arrange serial echo with left ventricular dimensions to time the operation
Discuss valve choice openly, balancing durability against lifelong anticoagulation
management.model: Heart team referral for valve surgery with blood pressure control, sport restriction, and serial dimension tracking

sources: ESC guideline on valvular heart disease, in own words
ASE guideline on valvular regurgitation, in own words
stem: A 44 year old engineering student from Pune reports exertional breathlessness and a pounding heartbeat at night. A collapsing pulse with a wide pulse pressure, an early diastolic murmur, and an Austin Flint rumble are found.
teaching: A collapsing pulse with a wide pulse pressure is the bedside flag for severe aortic regurgitation
Effective orifice 0.30 sq cm or more with volume 60 ml or more defines severe disease
Holodiastolic reversal in the descending aorta is the specific severe marker
Dilatation with symptoms sends the patient to the heart team for surgery timing
title: Severe chronic aortic regurgitation in a young adult
